title: Invertibility of the finite ordinary open restriction mate
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, an open immersion j:U→X, section-normalized coefficient operations o [def-sf-integral-open-operations], and a generator-normalized TensorComparison tensor. At any positive coefficient level indexed by n:N, transpose (tensor.ordinary n).inv under the ordinary integral-open and finite-open adjunctions. The resulting natural transformation finiteRestrictionMate: restriction⋙scalarReductionExtension_U(n) → scalarReductionExtension_X(n)⋙finiteRestriction(n) is invertible. No ordinary quotient model, strict system map, transition equation or system assembly is asserted.

source.place: Tags 03DJ and 0E8I, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0941, ordinary quotient construction.

proof.text: The scalar-reduction adjunction identifies its functor with the sheafified change-of-rings tensor, with unit x ↦ 1 tensor x. On the actual open slice, the sectionwise tensor presheaves have the same sections and balancing relations. Slice sheafification and the localized tensor comparison give inverse maps keeping each pure tensor.

Transport through o.integral and o.finite; their specified pushforward descriptions and projection square identify the scalar actions. Transpose the comparison under the finite-open adjunction. On every extension summand and scalar-unit generator, tensor.generators identifies it with inverse tensor comparison followed by the integral counit. Linearity, the tensor universal property, and the sheafification universal property extend the equality to all sections. The triangular identities identify the transpose as finiteRestrictionMate, so its components are isomorphisms.
